places.source_title: Waterfall — American Falls

places.name: Manitou Incline
places.recommendation: Joe Ferrucci and his friend Jordan set out to climb the Manitou Incline, billed on-screen as the tallest staircase in the United States. Jordan grinds his way up the relentless steps to the summit; Joe's own 'halfway through' update is filmed from a bar stool. A comedy bit, but an honest preview of how steep this climb is.
places.note: Geocoded as 'The Incline' (OSM, type: steps), Manitou Springs, El Paso County, CO.
places.source_title: Manitou Incline hike — 'Hold on I forgot something'

places.name: Eagle Tower
places.note: The reel says the views overlook Lake Michigan; the tower actually faces Green Bay (the bay between the Door Peninsula and mainland Wisconsin), with Horseshoe Island in view. Caption puts the park about a 5-hour drive from Chicago. The rebuilt tower (opened 2021) is reached by 95-100 stairs or an 850-foot accessible canopy ramp; Wisconsin DNR lists it open May 1-Oct 31.
places.recommendation: The reel's headline stop: add Peninsula State Park in Door County to a Wisconsin trip for Eagle Tower, reached by a long wooden elevated walkway through autumn trees to panoramic views over Green Bay and the surrounding islands — at their best in fall color. Parking, restrooms and park information are right at the tower area.
places.source_title: Fall colors — Eagle Tower, Peninsula State Park

additional_sources.recommendation: Asia's follow-up Peninsula State Park reel leads with Eagle Tower again: the elevated wooden boardwalk through peak autumn color out to the overlook above the water, pitched as the park's headline view on a Wisconsin trip about 5 hours from Chicago.
additional_sources.source_title: Peninsula State Park, Door County — a must-add Wisconsin trip

places.name: Eagle Trail
places.note: Pin is the Eagle Trail trailhead just west of the Eagle Tower parking area (Trailforks trailhead coordinates); DNR lists access at Eagle Terrace, Eagle Panorama or the Tower. DNR rates this 2.0-mile loop 'more difficult', with steep, rocky sections under 150-foot cliffs along Eagle Harbor.
places.recommendation: Shown in the reel right after the tower: the trailhead sign marked 'Difficult Trail' for the park's Eagle Trail, a loop the narrator points viewers to for more scenic overlooks beyond Eagle Tower.
places.source_title: Fall colors — Eagle Tower, Peninsula State Park

additional_sources.recommendation: The same reel shows the Eagle Trail trailhead sign (marked 'Difficult Trail') and points to the park's hiking trails as the way to explore beyond the tower.
additional_sources.source_title: Peninsula State Park, Door County — a must-add Wisconsin trip

He photographed the canyon completely dry on Nov 1, 2026, and in full flow the next day after the rain kept coming.
places.note: Pin is approximate: the ephemeral falls are not a mapped feature, so it sits on Kayenta Wash at the mouth of Hell Hole Canyon, just northwest of the Kayenta community in Ivins (OpenStreetMap). The falls flow only after heavy rain.

places.note: Access is by Havasupai Tribe reservation/permit only. Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.

places.name: Colchuck Lake
places.recommendation: Their candidate for the most beautiful lake in the USA: Colchuck Lake in the Enchantments outside Leavenworth. It's a 9-mile out-and-back with 2,340 ft of elevation gain (moderate-hard) — and extremely popular despite the effort. Their summer tip: get there extremely early; they arrived around 5 AM and the parking lot was nearly full, with 50+ cars along the road by the time they hiked out.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Most beautiful lake in the USA? — Colchuck Lake

additional_sources.recommendation: Jess's take on a trail that 'still manages to blow me away every time': the color of the water, the views of Dragontail Peak, and Aasgard Pass climbing into the Core Enchantments — 'worth every step.' 9 miles, about 2,400 ft of gain, and one hazard the other reel didn't mention: a very persistent mountain goat named Fred who disputes trail right-of-way.
additional_sources.source_title: Colchuck Lake — and a mountain goat named Fred

places.name: Kanab Sand Caves (Moqui Caverns)
places.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #1: caves carved into Navajo sandstone in the 1970s to harvest sand for glassmaking — now a free, photogenic scramble right off Highway 89, about 1.2 miles round trip with parking by the highway. Her caution: the scramble up can get a little scary; don't be afraid to turn back.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

places.name: Toquerville Falls
places.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #3: no hiking required if you have a 4x4 (don't attempt it in a normal car) — a 5.3-mile dirt road, about 45 minutes, to falls that pour over two pour-offs on La Verkin Creek: a cascade section and a clean 20-foot drop into a pool. Free BLM land, and the swimming is incredible in summer.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

places.name: Kanarra Falls
places.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #4 — her favorite of the five: a permitted slot-canyon waterfall hike, about 3.8 miles out and back with creek crossings the whole way and a ladder climb in the canyon. Permits sell out 1–2 weeks ahead in summer, so book early — and rent the waders unless you want numb feet for an hour afterwards.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

places.name: Water Canyon
places.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #5: a 4.25-mile out-and-back hike (about 500 ft of gain) that ends up looking like a mini version of Zion's Subway — and a pretty easy one. This is the one she says legit looks like the Subway.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.

places.name: Red Slot Canyon (Red Hollow)

places.note: The reel calls it 'Red Slot Canyon in Kanab' but its own access detail — park at the water facility at the end of Red Hollow Drive — identifies it as Red Hollow Slot Canyon near Orderville. Pin is the trailhead by the water tank; coordinates from two independent trail guides (37.2709, -112.6273), not OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

places.note: Two Bentonite Hills areas exist: the official ones inside Capitol Reef (Cathedral Valley) and the photographed BLM hills on Cow Dung Road near the Mars Desert Research Station outside Hanksville. Both source reels point to the Hanksville/MDRS hills (the 'none in a national park' list rules out the park site), so the pin uses the Cow Dung Road coordinates given by several independent guides (~38.4123, -110.7859).

additional_sources.recommendation: Megs and Pat's Mars-on-Earth pick: hills of bentonite clay near Hanksville, just outside Capitol Reef, striped purple, pink, red, orange, grey and blue-green from volcanic ash and minerals. Their practical notes: on the road toward the Mars Desert Research Station; unpaved access, high-clearance 4WD recommended; best at sunrise or sunset when low light brings out the colours; and never after rain — wet bentonite turns extremely slippery and sticky and vehicles get stuck.

places.name: Trappers Peak
places.recommendation: Gwyn and Ami's pick for some of the best panoramic mountain views in the North Cascades: Trappers Peak via Thornton Lakes — 9.7 miles with 3,438 ft of gain to stunning 360° summit views. Non-technical (no special gear or skills), with a few steep rock-scramble sections. Their tips: pack plenty of water (few places to filter), no backpacking on the peak itself, and Thornton Lakes backpacking is by competitive NPS permit.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Trappers Peak — 360° views of the North Cascades

places.name: Million Dollar Highway (US-550)
places.recommendation: American Travel Archives' 'you will NOT believe this road' drive: the Million Dollar Highway (US-550) from Ouray to Silverton — 25 miles through the San Juan Mountains famous for steep cliffs, tight switchbacks and few guardrails. Stop at Red Mountain Pass for the classic overlook; autumn is the best time, when golden aspens contrast with the red and gray rock. Their tips: drive it in good morning light, take your time at the pull-offs, and think twice in an RV. Ouray and Silverton bookend it with hot springs and silver-mining history.
places.note: Pin is at Red Mountain Pass, the highway's classic overlook (OpenStreetMap).
places.source_title: Million Dollar Highway (US-550) — Ouray to Silverton, CO

places.name: Spooky Gulch
places.recommendation: Jackie's verdict: 'TOTALLY worth it.' Spooky Gulch is the ultra-narrow Dry Fork slot canyon — the trailhead even has a metal frame you must fit through to enter. Inside: twisty sandstone walls, fun downclimbs, a sketchy up-climb to a section she calls 'INTO THE ARCHES', and squeezes so tight she had to take her backpack off and turn sideways.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Spooky Canyon in Utah!

places.name: Franconia Ridge Trail
places.recommendation: Calvin hiked the Franconia Ridge Trail in July — the classic above-treeline ridge walk across Little Haystack, Mount Lincoln and Mount Lafayette in Franconia Notch. His caution: check the weather and conditions before hiking it in fall or winter, and be prepared — the ridge is fully exposed.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Franconia Ridge Trail in New Hampshire

places.name: Cadillac Mountain
places.recommendation: Dave & Joce's pick for one of the most iconic sunrises in the U.S.: Cadillac Mountain, famous for being one of the first places in the country to see the sunrise during parts of the year. If you're driving up, vehicle reservations are required during the reservation season — or you can hike to the top.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Acadia's iconic sunrises — Cadillac Mountain & the Beehive

places.name: Snow Lake (Alpine Lakes)
places.recommendation: The Trekking Mama's 'how is this real?' lake: Snow Lake looks like it should require a plane ticket or a major expedition, but the trailhead is only about 60 minutes from Seattle. The water is an unbelievable bright alpine blue that looks photoshopped but isn't. It's popular and you'll share the trail — her tip is to keep going past the first viewpoints down toward the end of the lake, where the crowds thin out. Her go-to when someone visits Washington and needs a massive dose of alpine gorgeousness without planning a whole trip.
places.note: The Alpine Lakes Wilderness Snow Lake near Snoqualmie Pass — a different lake from the Snow Lake in Mount Rainier National Park, which is a separate pin. Pin is OpenStreetMap's named point for the lake.
places.source_title: Snow Lake — the 'how is this real?' lake an hour from Seattle

places.name: Cape Flattery
places.recommendation: The Griffins' verdict: even on a foggy day, Cape Flattery was unforgettable — the farthest northwest point of the Olympic Peninsula (and the contiguous U.S.), and one of those places that's worth going out of your way for.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap. Cape Flattery is on the Makah Reservation; a Makah recreation pass is required to visit.
places.source_title: Cape Flattery, Washington State

additional_sources.recommendation: Giselle calls it 'the final boss of PNW-maxxing' — the most northwestern place in the lower 48. The hike is 1.5 miles round trip with about 200 ft of gain: forest trails, boardwalks, stairs and multiple ocean viewpoints. A Makah Recreation Permit is required (online or in Neah Bay before the trailhead); open daily from dawn until 30 minutes after sunset, year-round. Her tips: it's a remote drive with spotty cell service, so download directions ahead, bring a rain jacket, and stay on the designated trails and viewing platforms.
additional_sources.source_title: Cape Flattery — the final boss of PNW-maxxing

places.name: Ice Lake Basin
places.recommendation: Calvin's pick: the Ice Lake Basin Trail outside Silverton, Colorado — the San Juan Mountains' famous alpine basin of electric-blue lakes (Ice Lake and Island Lake) ringed by 13,000-foot peaks.
places.note: Coordinates from published trail references for Ice Lake — the basin is not a mapped OpenStreetMap feature.
places.source_title: Ice Lake Basin Trail — Silverton, Colorado

places.name: Mesa Verde National Park
places.recommendation: Lindsay & Ryan: 'There's nowhere else on earth quite like this national park' — step back in time and explore the incredible cliff dwellings built by the Ancestral Pueblo people. Their plan: stay at Morefield Campground as the home base inside the park, start at the Visitor & Research Center to learn the history and plan the visit, book ranger-guided tours through Recreation.gov to get up close to the dwellings (they loved Cliff Palace and Balcony House), and grab fry bread at Soda Point after a day of exploring.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Mesa Verde — cliff dwellings, Cliff Palace & Balcony House

places.name: Cliff Palace
places.recommendation: The largest cliff dwelling in North America — and one of the two Mesa Verde dwellings Lindsay & Ryan loved exploring on a ranger-guided tour (booked through Recreation.gov to get up close).
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Mesa Verde — cliff dwellings, Cliff Palace & Balcony House

places.source_title: Mesa Verde — cliff dwellings, Cliff Palace & Balcony House

places.name: Tree of Life (Kalaloch Beach)
places.recommendation: Big Bat Billy's stop: the Tree of Life at Kalaloch Beach in Olympic National Park — the famous Sitka spruce that keeps growing over an eroded gully, its roots exposed in a root cave beneath it, right on the beach.
places.note: Coordinates from published references for the Tree of Life itself, at the north end of Kalaloch Beach by the campground — the tree is not a mapped OpenStreetMap feature (the beach's OSM point sits ~1.5 miles south).

places.name: Alvord Desert
places.recommendation: Jess drove 9 hours to camp on the Alvord Desert playa — under some of the darkest skies in Oregon — to teach herself astrophotography. She timed the trip under an almost-full moon by accident, so she waited for moonset, set a 3:24 AM alarm, and manually shot 105 long exposures (her old Sony has no intervalometer) to stitch a four-second starlapse. Her verdict: the Alvord had been on her list a long time and was worth every bit of the drive.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Alvord Desert — a 3:24 AM starlapse on the playa

places.name: Whipple's Cave
places.recommendation: A cave hiding in the Illinois woods: Whipple's Cave in Franklin Creek State Natural Area, reached via the Pioneer Pass Trail from the Mill Springs Day Use Area — 2.9 miles out and back with 226 ft of gain through wooded scenery, rocky terrain and creek crossings. Know before you go: be prepared for deep creek crossings, and other trails in the area also lead to the cave.

places.name: Mount Si
places.site: Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area
places.recommendation: WTA calls Mount Si the most popular hike in Washington — upwards of 100,000 hikers a year. The switchbacks start right at the trailhead; a mile and a half up you pass through Snag Flat, old-growth trees that survived fire and logging, then past a talus slope to the base of the Haystack, the true summit. 8.0 miles round trip with 3,150 ft of gain. Climbers training for Rainier haul heavy packs up here — the rule of thumb is that if you can make the top in under two hours, you're ready. A Discover Pass is required to park, and the lot fills early.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Mount Si — Washington's most popular hike

places.name: Wolf Creek Falls

places.name: Cataract Falls (Kenai Fjords)

places.note: Pin is at Cataract Cove in the Northwestern Fjord (OpenStreetMap) — the boat-tour stop named for its waterfalls, where the falls pour down the cove's cliffs into the sea.

places.name: Princess Arch
places.recommendation: A 1/4-mile walk on Princess Arch Trail (#233) to Princess Arch, a natural sandstone arch in Red River Gorge — the reel hikes it at peak fall color, with a sandstone ledge overlook above a valley of red and gold trees on the way.
places.note: Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's named Princess Arch point on Trail #233 (Wolfe County side of the gorge). Red River Gorge is in Daniel Boone National Forest; the creator's caption points to her series of 5+ Red River Gorge videos.

places.name: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park
places.recommendation: One of the most unique swims in the Midwest: hundreds of natural pools and chutes the Black River carved into billion-year-old volcanic rock — 'nature's own waterpark,' about 2 hours south of St. Louis. The reel's tips: go early in summer (it gets busy), wear water shoes for the slippery rock, and mind the stronger currents with kids.
places.note: Pin sits at the main shut-ins day-use area (OpenStreetMap point for the swimming area's supply store) rather than the park boundary centroid. The 'shut-ins' are narrow channels where the river squeezes through erosion-resistant rhyolite.
places.source_title: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park — nature's waterpark in Missouri

places.name: Wyalusing State Park
places.recommendation: 'This state park surprised us': 14+ miles of trails with caves to explore, an astronomy center that's perfect for stargazing, and four campgrounds on the bluffs near Bagley. Day pass $13 in-state / $16 out-of-state, per the reel.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's Wyalusing State Park point. The reel does not name the cave it films (stairs up a cliffside into a sandy-floored cave with lookout openings), so no cave name is recorded.
places.source_title: This state park surprised us — Wyalusing State Park, Wisconsin

places.name: Old Immigrant & Bluff Loop
places.recommendation: The creators' favorite trail in the park: the Old Immigrant & Bluff Loop — the hike the reel films, past a natural-arch rock formation and up wooden stairs built against the cliff to a cave with sandy floors, crawl spaces, and openings that look out over the forest.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's Old Immigrant Trail point within Wyalusing State Park.
places.source_title: This state park surprised us — Wyalusing State Park, Wisconsin

places.name: Hawk Hill
places.recommendation: It looks like Hawaii's Stairway to Heaven, but it's just north of San Francisco: an easy climb of about 650 steps from the parking area to panoramic views — the Pacific on one side, the Golden Gate Bridge on the other. No long hike, free parking off Conzelman Road.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's Hawk Hill peak point on Conzelman Road in the Marin Headlands (Golden Gate National Recreation Area); the reel's listed address is Hawk Hill, Conzelman Rd, Sausalito, CA 94965.
places.source_title: Hawk Hill — a 'Stairway to Heaven' viewpoint over the Golden Gate
5 Most Scenic Drives in California
places.name: Highway 395 (Eastern Sierra)
places.recommendation: One of Asya's five favorite California drives: Highway 395 along the Eastern Sierra — a winding road under snow-capped peaks and pine forests, with the Sierra escarpment on one side and the high desert on the other.
places.note: Pin at Lone Pine (OpenStreetMap village point), the classic Eastern Sierra stretch of US-395 beneath Mount Whitney; the drive itself runs the length of the Sierra's east side.

places.source_title: 5 Most Scenic Drives in California
places.name: 17-Mile Drive
places.recommendation: One of the five: the 17-Mile Drive through Pebble Beach — a tree-lined coastal road the reel shows bathed in golden sunset light, past cypress trees and ocean viewpoints.
places.note: Pin is an OpenStreetMap point on 17-Mile Drive itself in Pebble Beach (Del Monte Forest), on the Monterey Peninsula.

places.source_title: 5 Most Scenic Drives in California
places.name: Kings Canyon Scenic Byway
places.recommendation: One of the five: the Kings Canyon Scenic Byway — a narrow road carved between steep rocky canyon walls as it descends into Kings Canyon, following the Kings River toward Roads End.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's Kings Canyon Scenic Byway road point deep in the canyon (Highway 180).

places.source_title: 5 Most Scenic Drives in California
places.name: Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park
places.recommendation: One of the five: driving through Jedediah Smith Redwoods — a dense forest of towering old-growth redwoods, the reel's lush green counterpoint to the desert and coast drives.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's park point near Crescent City; the classic drive through the groves is Howland Hill Road.

places.source_title: 5 Most Scenic Drives in California

additional_sources.recommendation: Ranked #4 in Discover California's '7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you': 'McWay Falls, Pfeiffer Beach, Ewoldsen Trail, Partington Cove… it's almost impossible to pick a bad hike here.' Plan extra time, because you'll want to stop at every viewpoint.
additional_sources.source_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you

places.name: Big Sur (Highway 1)
places.recommendation: One of the five, and the caption's headliner: Big Sur — Highway 1 along green grassy cliffs above the Pacific and its rocky shoreline, the most famous coastal drive in California.
places.note: Pin at Bixby Creek Bridge (OpenStreetMap), the iconic span on the Big Sur stretch of Highway 1.

places.name: Seven Teacups
places.recommendation: A surreal chain of smooth white-granite pools on Dry Meadow Creek, each cup dropping 6 to 20 feet into the next before the water slides into the Kern River. Reached by a roughly 4-mile round-trip hike with about 850 feet of gain, rock scrambling and a creek crossing. The creator's warning, kept verbatim in spirit: please don't swim — the current can pull swimmers under even when the water looks calm.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's Seven Teacups waterfall point near Johnsondale Bridge, under 2 hours from Bakersfield. The reel names the AllTrails route 'Seven Tea Cups Viewpoint via Dry Creek Meadow' and mentions Johnny McNally's Fairview Lodge-Restaurant, about 10 minutes away, as a nearby stop (an amenity mention, not pinned).
places.source_title: Seven Teacups — granite pools above the Kern River

places.name: Torch Lake
places.recommendation: The 'Caribbean of the Midwest' in autumn: Torch Lake's turquoise, crystal-clear water and shallow sandbars ringed by peak fall color — the reel's drone shots show deep blue open water against shores of red and gold. The caption pitches the area's wineries and orchards as a perfect Michigan fall road trip.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's point for the long Torch Lake near Traverse City (Antrim County) — not the smaller Torch Lake in the Keweenaw Peninsula.
places.source_title: Torch Lake in Fall feels like the movies

places.name: Cape Kiwanda
places.best_for: Hike · Sand dune climb, tide pools and coastal views
places.recommendation: Climb the 240-foot sand dune for the payoff view over sandstone cliffs, tide pools and sandy beaches, with Pacific City's own Haystack Rock offshore. There's also an easier 1-mile walk along the beach to the rocks of the cape.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's point for the Cape Kiwanda headland.
places.source_title: Cape Kiwanda — 12/10 view on the Oregon Coast

places.name: Penn's Cave
places.best_for: Cave tour · America's only all-water cavern, toured by boat
places.recommendation: The reel's first stop: a boat ride through America's only all-water cavern — you float the underground river past illuminated stalactites instead of walking. It's also the only Pennsylvania cave on the National Register of Historic Places, with a wildlife park above ground.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2
places.note: Coordinates from the venue's published location, 222 Penns Cave Rd, Centre Hall (OpenStreetMap has no attraction point for the cave).

places.name: Bilger's Rocks
places.recommendation: A 300-million-year-old sandstone 'rock city' in Clearfield County — moss-covered boulders split into narrow passageways and small caves; the reel's presenter squeezes through the crevices and wanders the forest among the rocks.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2

places.name: Benezette Elk Viewing
places.recommendation: The reel stops in Elk County near Benezette for Pennsylvania's wild elk herd — wide fields at sunrise and sunset and a big bull elk filmed from the roadside. The Elk Country Visitor Center on Winslow Hill is the hub of the viewing area.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2
places.note: Pin is the Elk Country Visitor Center in Benezette, the center of the Winslow Hill elk-viewing area the reel films.

places.name: Pine Creek Gorge (PA Grand Canyon)
places.best_for: Scenic overlook · PA Grand Canyon overlooks and Turkey Path waterfall
places.recommendation: Tioga County's 'Grand Canyon of Pennsylvania' — a roughly 45-mile-long, 1,000-foot-deep forested gorge. The reel shows the rim overlooks at Leonard Harrison State Park, hikers on the cliff edges, and the Turkey Path trail dropping past its waterfall toward Pine Creek.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2

places.name: Wellsboro
places.best_for: Small town stop · Gas-lit Main Street and the Wellsboro Diner
places.recommendation: The reel's small-town stop: Wellsboro's historic, gas-lit Main Street, its storefronts and the classic Wellsboro Diner — the gateway town for the Pine Creek Gorge.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2

places.name: Austin Dam Ruins
places.best_for: Historic site · Ruins of the 1911 Austin Dam failure
places.recommendation: Honorable mention in the reel's caption: the towering concrete ruins of the Austin Dam in Potter County, which failed in 1911 and destroyed the town below — now a memorial park.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's Austin Dam Overlook viewpoint.

places.name: Kinzua Bridge State Park
places.best_for: Scenic overlook · Skywalk on the collapsed Kinzua Viaduct
places.recommendation: Honorable mention in the reel's caption: the Kinzua Viaduct in McKean County — once among the longest and highest railroad bridges in the world, toppled by a tornado in 2003 and reinvented as a skywalk out over the gorge, with the twisted towers still lying in the valley below.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2
places.note: The skywalk has been under intermittent repair closures scheduled through 2027, with seasonal openings — check the park page before going.

places.name: Hyner View State Park
places.best_for: Scenic overlook · West Branch Susquehanna vista and hang-glider launch
places.recommendation: Honorable mention in the reel's caption: a small Clinton County park built around one big view — the overlook (also a hang-glider launch) above a sweeping bend of the West Branch Susquehanna River.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2

places.name: Worlds End State Park
places.best_for: State park · Loyalsock Creek gorge park
places.recommendation: Honorable mention in the reel's caption: a rugged Sullivan County park in the Loyalsock Creek gorge — a swimming area on the creek, the Loyalsock Canyon Vista, and trailheads into Loyalsock Trail country.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2

places.name: Point Lobos
places.best_for: Hike · Turquoise coves, sea lions and coastal trails
places.recommendation: One of the most beautiful coastal parks in California — turquoise coves, sea lions, and some of the clearest ocean views you'll find anywhere. The reel warns it has become extremely popular: visit outside peak season and peak days for a more enjoyable experience.
places.source_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you

places.name: Armstrong Redwoods
places.recommendation: Walk among towering old-growth redwoods on mostly flat, easy trails — the magic of the redwoods without a strenuous hike.
places.source_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you

places.name: Mossbrae Falls
places.best_for: Waterfall · Springs pouring from a moss-covered cliff
places.recommendation: A breathtaking waterfall whose cascades pour straight out of a moss-covered cliff into the Sacramento River below.
places.source_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you
places.note: Access warning from the reel itself: reaching the falls requires walking along private, active railroad tracks, so visit only if you understand and accept the risks. AllTrails lists the route as closed / private property.

places.name: McWay Falls
places.best_for: Waterfall · 80-foot falls onto a Big Sur beach cove
places.recommendation: One of the four hikes the reel names under its #4 pick, 'literally anything in Big Sur': the 80-foot waterfall that drops onto the sand of McWay Cove, seen from the short Overlook Trail.
places.source_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you
places.note: AllTrails listed the Overlook Trail as closed in fall 2026 (fire damage); the falls remain viewable from Highway 1 pullouts — check current conditions.

places.name: Pfeiffer Beach
places.best_for: Beach · Purple-sand beach and Keyhole Rock
places.recommendation: One of the four spots the reel names under its #4 pick, 'literally anything in Big Sur' — the wild beach down Sycamore Canyon Road, famous for its purple-tinged sand and the Keyhole Rock arch.
places.source_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you

places.name: Ewoldsen Trail
places.best_for: Hike · Redwood canyon loop to coastal ridge views
places.recommendation: One of the four hikes the reel names under its #4 Big Sur pick: the loop up McWay Creek through redwood forest to open coastal ridge views — often called the best day hike in Big Sur.
places.source_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you
places.note: Pin is the Ewoldsen Trailhead at the park's main parking area. AllTrails listed the trail as closed in fall 2026 due to fire damage — check current conditions before going.

places.name: Partington Cove
places.best_for: Hike · Short trail through a rock tunnel to a hidden cove
places.recommendation: One of the four spots the reel names under its #4 Big Sur pick: a short, steep trail down through a hand-carved tunnel to a turquoise cove once used to load tanbark onto ships.
places.source_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you

places.name: Grizzly Creek Redwoods
places.recommendation: One of California's most underrated redwood groves, with peaceful trails and massive ancient trees but without the crowds of the more famous parks. The reel's fun fact: scenes from Star Wars were filmed here.
places.source_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you

places.name: Karl Knapp Trail
places.best_for: Hike · Flat redwood loop through ferns and moss
places.recommendation: The creator's favorite redwood hike of all time: a gorgeous, mostly flat loop (also signed as the Prairie Creek Trail) through a lush redwood forest filled with ferns, moss, and towering trees.
places.source_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you

places.name: Black Sands Beach
places.site: King Range National Conservation Area (Shelter Cove)
places.best_for: Beach · Black-sand beach — sunset and whale watching
places.recommendation: The reel's #1 pick: a dramatic black sand beach at Shelter Cove on the Lost Coast, surrounded by rugged cliffs and crashing waves. Time your visit for sunset, and if you're lucky you'll spot whales offshore; winter brings the dramatic moody weather shown in the reel.
places.source_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you

places.name: Cucumber Falls
places.best_for: Waterfall · 36-foot falls you can walk behind, on a 5-minute trail
places.recommendation: A beautiful waterfall you can stand inside of: a 36-foot bridal-veil falls on the Great Gorge Trail in Ohiopyle State Park, reached by a very short, super-maintained trail — under five minutes, with a scenic overlook at the start — that the creator stresses is easy enough for kids and elderly visitors. Scramble over the rocks at the base and you can walk behind the curtain of water.
places.source_title: Cucumber Falls — the waterfall you can stand inside

places.name: Massacre Rim
places.best_for: Stargazing · One of the darkest skies in America
places.recommendation: The carousel's Nevada pick: a wilderness study area so remote that the Milky Way stretches brilliantly across the sky on clear, moonless nights — among the darkest skies left in the United States.
places.source_title: You haven't really seen the night sky until you've visited places like these

places.name: Big Bend Ranch State Park
places.best_for: Stargazing · Vast desert with minimal light pollution
places.recommendation: The carousel's Texas pick: the sprawling state park west of Big Bend National Park, where vast desert landscapes and minimal light pollution create extraordinary stargazing.
places.source_title: You haven't really seen the night sky until you've visited places like these

places.name: Homestead Crater
places.best_for: Hot spring · Swim inside a 55-foot limestone crater
places.recommendation: A hidden underground hot spring inside a 55-foot-tall limestone crater: a naturally heated geothermal pool at 90–96°F year-round, about 65 feet deep, that you can soak, swim, snorkel or even scuba dive in. It's at the Homestead Resort in Midway, just outside Park City, but day visitors are welcome — $30 per person (the reel notes it was $15 when filmed) for a 60-minute session with about 40 minutes in the water; life jackets are required and provided, and reservations are recommended since weekends fill up.
places.source_title: There's a hidden underground hot spring in Utah… and you can swim inside it!

places.name: Tahoe Rim Trail
places.recommendation: The reel's opener: the 165-mile Tahoe Rim Trail, filmed on a narrow cliffside section high above Lake Tahoe's big blue water.
places.source_title: Epic USA hikes — how many have you done?
places.note: Pin sits on the trail's west-shore segment above Lake Tahoe; the 165-mile trail rings the lake across California and Nevada.

places.name: Devil's Head Lookout
places.best_for: Hike · Staffed fire lookout tower with 100-mile views
places.recommendation: Listed at 3 miles in the reel: the climb to the Devil's Head Lookout, the only Forest Service fire tower in Colorado still staffed — 143 stairs to the cab at 9,749 feet and views for 100 miles in every direction.
places.source_title: Epic USA hikes — how many have you done?

places.name: Chapel Loop Trail
places.best_for: Hike · 10-mile loop past two falls to Chapel Rock
places.recommendation: The reel's Michigan pick at 10 miles: the Chapel Loop in Pictured Rocks, past Mosquito Falls and Chapel Falls to Chapel Rock and the Lake Superior shoreline beaches.
places.source_title: Epic USA hikes — how many have you done?
places.note: Pin is Chapel Rock, on the loop's lakeshore section.

places.name: Skyline Loop Trail
places.best_for: Hike · Alpine loop to Panorama Point
places.recommendation: Listed at 6 miles in the reel: Rainier's signature loop from Paradise — wildflower meadows, Myrtle Falls, and the climb to Panorama Point with the mountain filling the sky.
places.source_title: Epic USA hikes — how many have you done?
places.note: Pin is the trailhead at Paradise, by the Jackson Visitor Center (trailhead coordinates from published trail guides).

places.name: Sahale Arm Trail
places.best_for: Hike · Ridge climb to the Sahale Glacier camp
places.recommendation: Listed at 12 miles in the reel: switchbacks up to Cascade Pass, then the steep climb along the Sahale Arm ridge through meadows — marmots and mountain goats along the way — to the Sahale Glacier camp, ringed by North Cascades peaks.
places.source_title: Epic USA hikes — how many have you done?
places.note: Pin is the Sahale Arm ridge (published place point); the trail starts at the Cascade Pass trailhead at the end of Cascade River Road.

places.name: Swiftcurrent Lake Trail
places.best_for: Hike · Easy lakeside loop in Many Glacier
places.recommendation: The reel's shortest pick at 2 miles: the easy nature-trail loop around Swiftcurrent Lake in Glacier's Many Glacier valley, under Mount Wilbur and past the historic Many Glacier Hotel.
places.source_title: Epic USA hikes — how many have you done?

places.name: Blue Lakes Trail
places.best_for: Hike · Three turquoise alpine lakes below Mt. Sneffels
places.recommendation: Listed at 10 miles in the reel: three stacked turquoise lakes — Lower, Middle and Upper Blue — in a glacial basin beneath 14,150-foot Mount Sneffels in the San Juan Mountains.
places.source_title: Epic USA hikes — how many have you done?
places.note: Pin is the Blue Lakes Trailhead (USFS listing, south of Ridgway); Lower Blue Lake is about 3.3 miles up the trail.

places.name: Cave of the Mounds
places.site: Cave of the Mounds National Natural Landmark
places.best_for: Cave tour · Underground formations near Madison
places.recommendation: A whole underground world near Madison: colorful rock formations, sparkling crystals and winding passages on guided tours offered year-round. The cave holds a steady 50°F, so bring a light jacket; it's a great family-friendly stop even on a rainy day, and the grounds above ground are worth exploring too.
places.source_title: A cave in Wisconsin? One of the coolest surprises near Madison

places.name: Green Lakes State Park
places.best_for: Meromictic lakes · Blue-green water without a major hike
places.recommendation: Two rare meromictic lakes — Green Lake and Round Lake — whose deep waters never mix seasonally, and whose unusual chemistry creates a striking blue-green color that looks like it should need a passport. Walk the easy shoreline trail, swim at the beach in season, kayak, or picnic — a few hours of exploring without needing a major hike.
places.source_title: I thought this shade of blue required a passport

places.name: Lake Clark
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.best_for: Scenic lake · The park's namesake turquoise lake
places.recommendation: One of the guide's named sights: the 42-mile turquoise lake at the heart of the park, ringed by volcanic peaks.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!

places.name: Proenneke Cabin
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.best_for: Historic site · Dick Proenneke's hand-built cabin at Twin Lakes
places.recommendation: One of the guide's named sights: the cabin Dick Proenneke built by hand at Twin Lakes and lived in for 30 years — now an NPS historic site, reached by floatplane.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!

places.name: Turquoise Lake
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.best_for: Scenic lake · Glacial turquoise backcountry lake
places.recommendation: One of the guide's named sights: a vivid turquoise glacial lake in the park's backcountry, beneath the Chigmit Mountains.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!

places.name: Port Alsworth
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.best_for: Gateway village · Park visitor center and trailheads
places.recommendation: One of the guide's named sights: the park's gateway village on Lake Clark's south shore — visitor center, air-taxi hub, and the trailhead for the Tanalian trail network.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!

places.name: Chinitna Bay
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.best_for: Bear viewing · Coastal brown bears on the Cook Inlet shore
places.recommendation: One of the guide's named sights: at the southern end of the park's Cook Inlet coast, where as many as twenty coastal brown bears can be visible from a single spot during the season.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!

places.name: Crescent Lake
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.best_for: Bear viewing · Salmon lake in the Chigmit Mountains
places.recommendation: One of the guide's named sights: a salmon lake in the heart of the Chigmit Mountains — sockeye and silver runs draw brown and black bears to the shoreline; most viewing is from boats, and visitors arrive by floatplane.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!
places.note: Pin is the Crescent Lake Ranger Station, whose coordinates NPS publishes; the lake is roadless with no developed trails.

places.name: Redoubt Volcano
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.recommendation: One of the guide's named sights: Mount Redoubt, the active stratovolcano dominating the park's Cook Inlet skyline (last erupted in 2009).
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!

places.name: Iliamna Volcano
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.recommendation: One of the guide's named sights (spelled 'Iliamana' in the caption): Mount Iliamna, the glacier-covered volcano at the park's southern end.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!

places.name: Telaquana Lake
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.best_for: Scenic lake · Remote lake on the historic Telaquana Trail
places.recommendation: One of the guide's named sights: a remote lake on the historic Telaquana Trail route across the park's northern backcountry.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!

places.name: Tanalian Falls
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.best_for: Hike / Waterfall · 4.3 mi, moderate (per the guide)
places.recommendation: One of the guide's best hikes: the 4.3-mile moderate trail from Port Alsworth to a waterfall on the Tanalian River, in the shadow of Tanalian Mountain.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!

places.name: Kontrashibuna Lake
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.recommendation: One of the guide's best hikes: the 4.3-mile moderate hike from Port Alsworth to this long lake east of town, with Tanalian Mountain views.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!

places.name: Tanalian Mountain
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.recommendation: One of the guide's best hikes: the 9.6-mile hard climb up the 3,800-ft peak that towers over Port Alsworth and Lake Clark.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!

places.name: Beaver Pond Loop
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.recommendation: One of the guide's best hikes: a 3.5-mile easy loop from Port Alsworth through spruce forest to a beaver pond — the park's gentlest trail.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!
places.note: Pin is Port Alsworth, where the loop starts by the visitor center.

places.name: Teetering Rock
places.site: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
places.recommendation: One of the guide's best hikes: a 1.8-mile moderate hike in the Tanalian trail network out of Port Alsworth, to a giant boulder balanced above the trail.
places.source_title: Save these places for Lake Clark National Park!
places.note: Pin is on the Tanalian Falls trail, the route this short hike follows out of Port Alsworth.

places.name: Needles Eye Tunnel
places.best_for: Scenic drive · One-lane tunnel carved through granite
places.recommendation: The Needles Highway through Custer State Park winds between towering granite spires until the road tightens and passes through the Needles Eye Tunnel — a one-lane tunnel hand-carved through solid granite in the 1920s, one of the most photographed drives in the Black Hills. Know before you go: the tunnel is about 8'4" wide and 12' tall, one vehicle at a time, and RVs/trailers should avoid the route; drive it early morning or late afternoon for fewer cars and better light, and watch for bison, pronghorn and prairie dogs nearby.
places.source_title: This state park drive feels unreal the first time you see it
